about: Per-jurisdiction PRESCRIPTIVE ROOFTOP-PV PATHS, as data (review-audit draft 14). permitPath.ts reads these records with one generic rule and names no state. A record says the jurisdiction publishes the prescriptive-vs-engineered SPLIT (`split`: two applications, the AHJ takes exactly one): its screen `limits`, its `roofingRow` (the coverings and layer counts its prescriptive path admits, with the row's own words), the `code` the words cite and the `displayName` they use. A STATE record (ahj empty) applies to a job whose state normalises to `state` (usStateCode; an unrecognised spelling matches nothing and the path asks). An AHJ record (ahj set) applies inside its state when the job's AHJ contains one of `ahjNames` (lower-case substring) and wins over the state record. Limits: a job with a record is screened on the record's limits; a PERSON-VERIFIED (or official) jurisdiction_code_profiles row's stated limits overlay them field by field (rule 3), a seeded profile never does. A job with no record keeps the existing rule: its own researched hasPrescriptivePath decides, else the standard structural review. `criteriaDefault` marks the record whose limits sit underneath evaluatePrescriptiveCriteria when a caller asks for defaults (the strictest full set on file). Nothing here blocks on its own: a failed screen routes the path, as before.

records.source: Oregon BCD Form 440-5952 (Prescriptive Solar PV Installation Checklist)

roofingRow.name: the BCD 5952 roofing row
roofingRow.admits: only metal, single-layer wood shingles/shakes, or <=2-layer composition
roofingRow.layersLimit: no more than two layers of composition (one of wood shingles/shakes)
